title: Armstrong forgets to introduce him at Boston's Symphony Hall
summary: Armstrong usually introduced hometown players, but Russell had to remind him at Boston's Symphony Hall before he called Holmes 'Pickles'.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Maybe you could mention a little bit about how it was when you were out with Louis Armstrong, and whenever you got to somebody's... When there was a member of the band and you got to their home town, Louis would mention...
Well, he would always introduce... In anybody's home town we went to, he would always introduce this person to the audience, and let them know that one of

their own boys was in the orchestra. So we happened to play my home town, which happened to be Boston, Massachusetts. And we were playing in one of the most dedicated spots in Boston, which was the Symphony Hall, where the Boston Symphony Orchestra plays all the time. So we were playing there. We're the special... We're not playing symphonic music; we're playing dance music.

So okay, we set up there, and we're playing, and I see a lot of my friends come in, they're waving their hand at me and running up and shaking my hands, and this-that-and-the-other. So I'm sitting back, waiting for the big moment when Louis is going to introduce me. So the night goes on and on and on. And it looked like he wasn't going to introduce me! So I looked over to Russell, and I says... One of those things, you know.

So Luis Russell calls Louis Armstrong over to him, and he told him, "This is Charlie's home town." He said, "Oh, I'm sorry..." -- he called Pickles. Louis would call me Pickles. He says, "I'm sorry Pickles. Yeah. Man, folks, we have one of your home boys here, Charlie 'Pickles' Holmes" -- and made me take a bow. I mean, they give me a big hand, and one thing and another. It made me feel good. But I don't know, it could have been better.
Well, it had just slipped his mind, because...
Yeah, it had slipped his mind.
Yes, because of the time Louis was very generous about trying to bring other people to the fore.
Very much so. It really had slipped his mind. I mean, he hadn't given it a thought, really. Because he didn't do it maliciously or anything like that.
